title: Rebuilding CI for AI-Scale Commit Volume — Gautam Korlam, Sonar
talk_summary: Gautam Korlam (ex-Uber, now Sonar) argues that CI and review queues built for human commit rates become the bottleneck once agents open many PRs, and that individually-green PRs can still break trunk when merged together. He proposes faster/sharded/cached CI, shifting checks left, AI-first review with policy-based auto-approval, and recording durable audit records (agent identity, session, test reports, finding resolution, non-self-approval) on every PR.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of serializing merges or letting everything merge, they test likely combinations of in-flight commits in parallel, evict PRs predicted to break, and only land commits that pass against the combined set.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we tested all the likely possibilities of commits that are coming in ... only if it passes with all the combination of commits coming in it would be let into go directly onto the trunk
takeaways.numbers: serialized merge would take ~20 days to go green at Uber's volume

takeaways.technique: Make CI incremental and cached so repair loops are cheap
takeaways.what_they_do: Cache build outputs, reduce compiler invalidation churn, shard tests, and remove expensive checks from the pre-merge path (moving them post-merge) so incremental CI is near-instant once warm.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're able to bring the time of CI almost like less than a minute for incremental steps, which means once the cold CI is warmed up, incremental builds are way way quick quicker
takeaways.numbers: ~10 min baseline CI reduced to <1 min for incremental steps

takeaways.technique: Policy-based auto-approval with escalation for sensitive paths
takeaways.what_they_do: Define plain-English approval policies: auto-approve low-risk changes (docs, dependency bumps, internal tooling), require human/extra approver for sensitive areas (payments, auth), and forbid an agent from approving its own change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't want to have the agent who made the change approve its change because that would not be uh zero trust

takeaways.technique: Durable audit record on the PR instead of expiring CI artifacts
takeaways.what_they_do: Record on the PR: which agent made it, originating session/prompt, trusted commit + saved test report (not just status), how each finding was resolved, who approved (not the author's prompter), and reasons for any overridden checks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what is a commit where CI was trusted and a save test report, not just a status? And making sure that each finding has like a record of how it was resolved

takeaways.technique: AI-first review pass, humans/agents only on the residue
takeaways.what_they_do: Run automated review as the first pass so human (or higher-tier) review only sees what AI left unresolved, and have the reviewing agent suggest and commit fixes with the engineer as co-author.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have an agent on CI iterate and fix and humans are able to review whatever is left after the AI took its first pass
takeaways.numbers: 13% of PRs had a recorded CI failure requiring a repair round-trip

takeaways.technique: Shift checks left into the agent's local context
takeaways.what_they_do: Move as many checks as possible earlier (into the agent's local run) because it's cheaper to catch there and the agent already has the context to fix it immediately.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you can move them to the left, it's way cheaper to catch them ... locally, agents have done more context anyway to fix the issue
